text:
maria: FYI — customer reported repeated mid-stream disconnects on SSE when their Android app switches from office Wi‑Fi to cellular. They say it happens reliably after ~12–18s into a long response. Attached logs from their device and our proxy below.

alex: Thanks — do we have the original client logs (stack traces / tcp dumps)? Any common token refresh or 401 around the time?

maria: They pasted the logs — no 401s. Looks like TLS session resets then a stream `502` seen in our proxy. Customer says reconnect flow shows a new stream started but missing the last few events. Pasting sanitized logs: 

```
Client: GET /v1/stream?model=gpt-internal HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Accept: text/event-stream
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Connection: keep-alive

[12s later] recv: partial chunk 
[13s] tls: read: connection reset by peer
[13s] client: reconnect attempt with Last-Event-ID: evt-42
[13s] server: 502 Bad Gateway (nginx upstream prematurely closed connection)
```

jordan: I attempted to reproduce on Pixel 6 (Android 13) by toggling Wi‑Fi off while SSE active. I see the TCP connection gets an immediate RST from the phone's OS when it flips networks (mobile dataplan). The server logs show `upstream prematurely closed connection` and later an `ALB: 502` spike correlating to the time window.

kevin: tagging infra — this smell is ALB/NGINX proxy timeout + client-side abrupt socket teardown during network handover. On mobile the TCP stack often issues RST when interface goes down, which causes the proxy to see a close mid-stream. If the proxy already buffered some chunks, upstream may abort.

sre-bot: ALERT: cluster-hosted-us-east-2 saw a +1.8% 502 rate in /v1/stream between 2026-03-12T14:00 and 2026-03-12T14:10 — correlated with mobile client reconnection patterns. See infra ticket INFRA-421.

maria: Customer asked if we can guarantee at-least-once delivery or reassembly of partial outputs. They currently lose last ~200 tokens on reconnect.

alex: We don't have exactly-once semantics for streaming; best-effort. Recommended mitigations: client should use `Last-Event-ID` and server should be able to resume from that ID if possible (idempotent checkpoints), or send periodic event checkpoints. Interim server-side mitigations: increase ALB idle timeout, reduce proxy buffer timeouts, and avoid buffering entire chunk in nginx (proxy_buffering off).

kevin: Actionable repro steps for infra/eng: 
1) Reproduce locally using `tc` to simulate network interface drop: `tc qdisc add dev wlan0 root netem loss 100%` then kill interface.
2) Curl SSE test (no buffering) to reproduce stream drop behavior: 
```
curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  'https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=test'
```
3) On server side run tcpdump to capture the RST: `sudo tcpdump -n -i any 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-rst) != 0' -w rst.pcap`

jordan: I ran the curl test on a tethered phone and toggled airplane mode. I captured a client-side RST and an immediate `upstream prematurely closed connection` in nginx. Enabling `proxy_ignore_client_abort off;` didn't change behavior — nginx still saw upstream killed.

ops-liaison: From a support process POV, we should tell customer: 1) implement Last-Event-ID reconnect and exponential backoff, 2) consider short lived checkpoint events every ~50 tokens so reconnect can resume closer to the last point, 3) we'll investigate infra tweaks to reduce impact.

maria: Customer asked whether auth token rotation could be a culprit — I verified their token doesn't refresh during the session window. No `401`.

kevin: For infra follow-ups I'm proposing a small config change rollout:
- ALB: increase idle timeout from 60s -> 180s for streaming routes
- nginx: `proxy_read_timeout` -> 240s and `proxy_buffering off` for `/v1/stream` location
- Add server-side periodic pings (SSE comment heartbeats `:ping\n\n`) every 10s to keep mobile NAT pinholes alive

alex: Also adding a short-term monitoring alert for a >0.5% increase in 502s from streaming endpoints; ops to watch during the config rollout.

sre-bot: NOTE: created infra change request CR-1234 for ALB/nginx config updates and INFRA-421 linked.

maria: Customer has a production window tomorrow 08:00 PST. They asked if we can do a hotfix. Kevin — can infra cut a canary with the new timeouts in us-east-2?

kevin: Yes — will schedule a canary during low traffic window, and we'll roll back if 502s increase. I'll coordinate with ops-liaison and paste the runbook here when scheduled.

alex: Follow-up checklist: 
- [ ] Repro on emulated mobile handover (jordan)
- [ ] Canary ALB/nginx patch (kevin)
- [ ] Add SSE resume docs & sample client logic to support team (maria)
- [ ] Notify customer and provide workaround (maria)

ops-liaison: I'll own timeline and comms. Drafting message to customer now with suggested client changes + expected infra window.

maria: Thanks all — I'll update CASE-1029 & link CR-1234/INFRA-421. Leaving thread open for canary results. :eyes:
